classification: independently authored static source semantics; not an executable or GUI case
named_question: Can the LightController2 pre-modal preparation change scene or other persisted members even when the subsequent dialog is cancelled?
answer: Yes, conditionally. The preparation writes the original controller, not only the temporary dialog. It can assign channel names, capabilities and the name mask, retag existing scene Q values, and reinitialize a channel of an existing SID 777 scene. These operations precede the dialog snapshot and modal result. Cancel skipping accepted-only copy-back is not a whole-document no-op guarantee.

transaction_order: Run preparation against the original controller.
If preparation returns nonzero, call the owner notification at virtual offset +0x238 before the modal call.
Copy the now-prepared controller names, scene collection and other selected data into the dialog.

Reuse the previously recovered accepted-only copy-back/post-hook contract. Other modal returns skip that copy-back; this callsite has no explicit restoration of the preparation's original-member writes.
A later independent save may serialize the prepared members; no save or successful disk persistence is implied by preparation or cancel.

conditional_effects.common_gate: For index i, find the controller output connector and a referencing object through 0x140453870 and 0x1404ff730. Enter the update body only when a referencing object exists and either the stored channel name is empty or the connector exists with its 32-bit member +0x128 equal to zero.
conditional_effects.ordinary_unparented_object: With no object at reference+0xc8 and reference type neither 0x140 nor 0x163, this call's -1 mode assigns the reference label at +0x2b8, falling back to +0x58 when empty. This branch does not execute its nonnegative-mode scene retagging or SID 777 initializer.
conditional_effects.special_unparented_type_0x163: Assign the same label/fallback. If the connector+0x128 gate is true and the reference's virtual +0x4b0(0) connection list contains the identity returned by controller virtual +0x4b0(0x33+i), replace the top nibble of each in-range existing scene Q with 4, preserving its low 28 bits. This branch does not call the SID 777 initializer.
conditional_effects.parent_or_type_0x140: Use the object at reference+0xc8 when present, otherwise the type-0x140 reference itself. Compute a candidate label through 0x1405c1380. If the current channel name is empty, assign that label and, when its classification result is zero, OR bit i into COName. Regardless of whether the name was empty, assign CapAI<i> from reference virtual +0x7a8, retag each in-range existing scene Q with the low four bits returned by the selected object's virtual +0xc68, then call 0x1405ccb60(controller,i). The initial common gate still applies.
conditional_effects.existing_sid_777: The last helper searches the existing scene vector for SID 777. If found and index i is in its primary vector, it replaces that one Q value with a type-dependent default payload and the scene's current top nibble. It does not create SID 777. Thus this branch can change the low 28 bits too, not only retag a scene.
conditional_effects.other_members: No explicit scene-count, scene-Outputs, identity, primary-vector resize, secondary-vector or SeqConf write was found in the preparation body or its inspected SID 777 initializer. This is a bounded explicit-write observation under the helper assumptions, not heap purity.
conditional_effects.return_value: A nonzero result reports an update path, not a byte-difference proof: an assignment can write a value equal to its previous value.

assumptions: Frozen static normal-return dataflow; valid objects, successful allocations and consistent in-range vectors.
Member/string/vector helpers operate on their indicated objects; the stack-local reference-count vector passed to 0x1404e56e0 is not a controller scene vector.
Graph traversal, label classification and virtual getter callbacks return normally, with no reentrant document edits or unexpected aliases into scene storage.
Ordinary dialog destruction is cleanup, not an undisclosed rollback of the original controller. No claim is made about unrelated owner/UI callbacks.
No global heap-purity, reentrancy-safety, complete native graph/XML equivalence, GUI behavior, successful save, or runtime parity is established.
Export completeness describes available recovered functions, not semantic or GUI parity.
remaining_dependencies_for_xml_diagnosti: Establish which actual XML graph yields the reference selected by 0x1404ff730, including object+0xc8 parent identity and native traversal/first-match behavior.
Establish the exact native output-connector instance/alias and XML/default initialization supplying its +0x128 word; no diagnostic infers the common gate from an empty XML name alone.
Resolve the concrete runtime-class targets/results of reference virtual +0x7a8 and selected-object virtual +0xc68 for any proposed XML diagnostic.
For the type-0x163 countercase, establish the runtime +0x4b0 connection lists and identity equality checked against controller slot 0x33+i.
These dependencies bound XML prediction, not the recovered fact that direct original-member writes precede the modal result.

cli_decision.reason: The native conditional stored-member effects are established, but complete XML-to-native graph/alias preconditions are not. A broad cancel-risk diagnostic would overclaim.
